title: Vayakhel: wise-hearted spinners (Exodus 35:25–26)
hookLine: women whose hearts stirred them spun the goats' hair with skill

cards: Goat hair is not glamorous. It's coarse, it smells like goat, and it's hard to work.

But the sanctuary needed it: a tent of goat-hair cloth stretched over the beautiful inner curtains, taking the sun and the dust and the wind so the rest could stay fine. Somebody had to spin it into yarn.
The Torah could have just said it was done. Instead, it stops to tell us who did it, and what moved them to do it.

teach.b: In the JPS 1917 translation: "And all the women that were wise-hearted did spin with their hands." They brought blue and purple and scarlet yarn, and fine linen.
Then the next verse: "And all the women whose heart stirred them up in wisdom spun the goats' hair." Twice in two verses, wisdom sits in the heart.
In Hebrew such a woman is chachmat lev, wise of heart, the Torah's phrase for a skilled person. The heart in biblical Hebrew is where people think and choose, not only where they feel.
So a skilled hand starts in a wise heart.
Rashi adds a detail from the Talmud that's hard to picture: these women spun the hair while it was still on the goats, and he calls it an exceptional art.
The Torah never gives their names, but it credits them right there in the building story, alongside Bezalel and the craftsmen.

Look back over this week: the building stopping for Shabbat, Moses in the cleft of the rock, the thirteen attributes, Moses gathering the people again, gifts so many the builders said stop, mirrors turned into a basin.
And now, women spinning coarse hair with wise hearts, for the tent that would take the weather. The sanctuary isn't only gold.
It's also goat hair, spun by people whose names we'll never know, and whose skill the Torah made sure to record.

how: The Torah's phrase for a skilled craftsperson is wise of heart (chacham lev, or chachmat lev for a woman), and the women spinners of Exodus 35 are read about each year in the portion Vayakhel.

games.q: the sanctuary's outer tent needs yarn from coarse goats' hair: hard, smelly work. how does the Torah describe the people who did it?
o: women whose hearts stirred them up in wisdom.
games.why: all the women whose heart stirred them up in wisdom spun the goats' hair. the Torah records their skill and their willing hearts.

practice: Think of a person whose work holds things together without anyone noticing: the one who always knows where everything is, the one who calms a room.
Picture their hands at work, and name the skill exactly, as if you were writing it into the Torah's list.
